prompt:
Return exactly one bare JSON object with keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country". Every key is required and every value is a string or JSON null. No extra keys, Markdown, or prose.

Isolate the source. The user message is a short note containing one contact block. Use only that block's label/value lines; recognize label variants and colon, equals, or tab separators. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Never derive values from email domains or company suffixes. Trim each value and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing values are null except for the international-phone country fallback below.

Assign before rendering. Reserve the country line for country. Assign a value containing @ to email. Assign a value to phone if, after dropping a leading tel: and any trailing extension (ext., ext, x, #, or extension followed by digits), it contains at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . /. Use content even when the labels are swapped. If the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not, swap those values before removing the suffix. The legal suffix list, matched case-insensitively at the end, is: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Resolve country and phone together. Convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, accepting English, Swedish, and German names and alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes in any case. Accept common aliases: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ. Classify the phone after removing tel: and its extension: ignoring an opening parenthesis, an initial + or 00 makes it international. For international numbers, change initial 00 to +, remove (0), then remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code even when it disagrees with the country line. If country is missing, infer it from an international phone only if the calling code belongs to a single country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For national numbers, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code. Without a country, return null for a national phone. A non-null phone is E.164: + followed only by the calling code and national significant number in digits.

Render text fields. For a comma-form name, split at the first comma and put the first-name portion before the last-name portion. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, with or without a dot and in any case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated name part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; do not transliterate. For company, remove the trailing legal suffix and any optional comma immediately before it, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. For email, remove the mailto: prefix and enclosing angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.

Before returning the object, recheck every null against the assigned record values and the phone and country rules. Do not guess or use any other source.
